13508.long: Masses picked off Justin Herbert in the first and fourth quarters, helping the Raiders secure an upset over a division rival. The fifth-round rookie put together a stellar performance while playing 73 percent of the defensive snaps in Sunday's contest, likely securing himself the starting cornerback role in Darien Porter's (foot) absence.

8266.short: Walker logged 10 tackles (five solo) in Sunday's 26-14 win over the Chargers.
8266.long: Walker's 10 total tackles tied fellow linebacker Nakobe Dean for most on the team in Sunday's contest. The inside linebacker played all 67 defensive snaps in the game, his second time in as many games with a 100.0 percent snap share. Walker now has 16 tackles (seven solo) through two regular-season games in 2026.

13269.short: Mendoza did not play a single snap during the Raiders' 26-14 win over the Chargers on Sunday.
13269.long: As expected, Mendoza observed Sunday's win from the sidelines as Kirk Cousins led the offense, with the veteran quarterback competing 19 of 29 passes for 253 yards, three touchdowns and one interception. Cousins has led the Raiders to a 2-0 start and should remain as the starter moving forward, but Mendoza could take over under center if the team's winning ways don't last.

8180.short: Nailor caught one of three targets for nine yards in Sunday's 26-14 win over the Chargers.
8180.long: Nailor's three targets were fourth on the team, and he continues to run plenty of routes. The production is lacking through two games, as Nailor has just four catches for 36 scoreless yards on eight targets. Cody White secured a pair of touchdowns as the fourth wideout Sunday, and it will be interesting to see if White starts getting more snaps at Nailor or Jack Bech's expense.

13305.short: Washington rushed three times for seven yards while failing to catch his only target during Sunday's 26-14 win over the Chargers.
13305.long: Washington was far less efficient with his carries in Week 2, averaging 2.3 YPC after he turned seven carries into 41 yards against the Dolphins in the team's regular-season opener. The running back operated as a distant No. 2 option in the backfield, as Ashton Jeanty logged 21 carries for 48 yards while catching four of seven targets for 15 yards. Washington is nothing more than a bench stash option in fantasy leagues at the moment.

12509.short: Harris caught six of seven targets for 76 yards during Sunday's 24-16 loss to Buffalo.
12509.long: Harris led the team in targets, receptions and receiving yards in the loss, all of which represented new career highs for the second-year pro. The wide receiver has now reeled in 10 of 16 targets for 149 yards over three games to open the regular season, and he appears to be on track to be a pivotal member of the team's passing attack in 2026.

9511.short: Mitchell rushed eight times for 52 yards and caught all three of his targets for minus-5 yards and a touchdown during Sunday's 24-16 loss to the Bills.
9511.long: Mitchell found himself far move involved on offense in Week 3, nearly matching his previous season total of nine carries while the three targets matched a career high. The running back reached paydirt in the first quarter, reeling in a one-yard pass from quarterback Justin Herbert. Mitchell remained the team's second option out of the backfield behind starter Omarion Hampton, but he proved that he could have standalone fantasy value if he gets more consistent touches moving forward.

8259.short: Dicker went 3-for-4 on field-goal attempts and made his lone extra-point try during the Chargers' 24-16 loss to the Bills on Sunday.
8259.long: Dicker's made field goals came from 33, 21 and 33 yards, with his miss early in the second quarter coming from 45 yards. Dicker has missed two of his five field-goal attempts through the first three games of the regular season, well below the 90 percent success rate he enjoyed in each of the first four years of his NFL career.

6797.short: Herbert completed 20 of 34 passes for 226 yards with one touchdown and one interception and rushed four times for 17 yards in the Chargers' 24-16 loss to the Bills on Sunday.
6797.long: Herbert finished with some serviceable numbers, but his play-to-play consistency lacked at times in a tough road environment. The 2020 first-round pick connected with a relatively narrow pool of six targets, and his one touchdown throw came via a shovel pass to Keaton Mitchell to cap off the opening drive of the game. Herbert also saw what was originally ruled a lost fumble returned for a touchdown reversed just before the two-minute warning, and through three games, he's completed only 59.1 percent of his passes while mustering a 3:4 TD:INT during an alarmingly winless start to the season for the Chargers. Herbert and his teammates draw a second straight unenviable assignment in Week 4, as they travel to face the defending champion Seahawks next Sunday afternoon.

11635.short: McConkey secured four of five targets for 66 yards in the Chargers' 24-16 loss to the Bills on Sunday.
11635.long: Justin Herbert's top target turned in a solid stat line in the Chargers' third straight loss to open the season, yet it still wasn't enough to net Los Angeles its first win. McConkey finished second in receptions and receiving yards while slotting in third in targets on the afternoon for the Bolts, but through three contests, he sports a modest 12-183-1 line on 15 targets. It doesn't get any easier for the Chargers in Week 4, as they pay a visit to the defending champion Seahawks next Sunday afternoon.

12507.short: Hampton rushed 15 times for 56 yards and failed to bring in his only target in the Chargers' 24-16 loss to the Bills on Sunday.
12507.long: The Chargers' No. 1 back got seven more carries than change-of-pace option Keaton Mitchell, but he was able to outpace the latter by only four yards. It was a disappointing downturn for Hampton, who'd broken out with 94 rushing yards and a touchdown while adding a 2-21-0 receiving line against the Raiders in Week 2. The Chargers are now alarmingly 0-3 heading into a daunting Week 4 road matchup against the Seahawks, but Hampton figures to remain in a clear-cut lead role for that contest.

13633.short: Shelley (hamstring) is active Week 3 against the Bills.
13633.long: Shelley was at risk of missing his first game of the season after sitting out practice Thursday, but he returned on a limited basis Friday and ended up getting cleared to play. The undrafted free agent has primarily served on special teams to start his career, and he did pick up his first two career tackles in Week 2 against the Raiders. He'll be slotted for a similar role this week in Buffalo.

12901.short: The Chargers elevated Herbert from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday ahead of Sunday's game against the Bills.
12901.long: Herbert is set to be the No. 3 tight end behind Oronde Gadsden and Hayden Rucci in Sunday's contest due to the absences of Charlie Kolar (forearm) and David Njoku (lower leg). The tight end is set to suit up alongside his brother and quarterback Justin Herbert. The duo could combine for the first brother-to-brother completion in NFL regular-season history while quarterback legend Tom Brady is on the call.

10898.short: Tuipulotu (hamstring) does not carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against the Bills.
10898.long: A hamstring injury limited Tuipulotu's practice participation Wednesday and Thursday, but he was a full participant in Friday's session, which was enough for him to avoid an injury tag for Week 3. The fourth-year pro has not logged a sack through the first two games of the regular season after recording a career-high 13.0 sacks across 16 regular-season games in 2025.

4971.short: James (finger) was a full participant in Thursday's practice.
4971.long: James broke his pinky finger during the Chargers' Week 2 loss to the Raiders, but the veteran safety was on the field for Thursday's session with a cast on, per Kris Rhim of ESPN.com. James is track to play in Sunday's road game against the Bills, though it's unclear whether he will don the cast for that contest. He's logged 17 tackles (nine solo) and one pass defense through the first two games of the 2026 regular season.

8519.short: Leonard (abdomen) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice.
8519.long: Leonard missed the Chargers' Week 2 loss to the Raiders with an abdominal issue after practicing in limited fashion during the week. The upgrade in practice participation means Leonard has likely overcome the issue and should be healthy enough to suit up for Sunday's game against the Bills.

5086.short: Valdes-Scantling was signed to the Chargers' active roster Wednesday.
5086.long: Valdes-Scantling inked a deal to join the practice squad with Los Angeles on Sept. 15, and he will now get a shot with the active roster. The 31-year-old will provide the team with another veteran option at wide receiver ahead of Week 3 versus the Bills.

4033.short: The Chargers placed Njoku (fibula) on injured reserve Wednesday.
4033.long: Njoku will be sidelined for at least the Chargers' next four games after sustaining a fibula injury in Sunday's 26-14 loss to the Raiders. Fellow tight end Charlie Kolar (forearm) was able to avoid placement on IR but has already been ruled out for the Chargers' Week 3 contest in Buffalo, leaving Oronde Gadsden as the top option on the depth chart heading into that game.

3271.short: Higbee caught eight of 11 targets for 62 yards and a touchdown during Sunday night's 30-26 loss to the Broncos.
3271.long: Higbee went from having no targets in Week 2 to leading the team with eight catches while finishing second only to wide receiver Davante Adams (13) in targets one week later. The tight end reeled in his first touchdown of the year to cap off the team's second possession of the game, connecting with quarterback Matthew Stafford for a five-yard score. Higbee may have seen the added opportunities as a result of fellow tight end Terrance Ferguson sustaining an ankle injury in the first quarter, but Ferguson was able to return to action. Higbee will have a chance to prove that his performance wasn't an anomaly when the team hosts Philadelphia in Week 4.

12718.short: Mumpfield caught four of eight targets for 93 yards and a touchdown during Sunday night's 30-26 loss to Denver.
12718.long: Mumpfield operated in a more prominent role at wide receiver behind Davante Adams once again in Week 3 while Puka Nacua (hip) remained sidelined for a second game in a row. The 23-year-old finished third on the team in targets behind Adams (13) and tight end Tyler Higbee (11). Mumpfield's biggest moment of the game came in the fourth quarter when he connected with quarterback Matthew Stafford for a 48-yard score with 3:46 remaining in regulation. The wide receiver has opened the campaign by catching five of 11 targets for 105 yards and a touchdown through three regular-season contests.

11586.short: Corum rushed six times for 15 yards and caught two of four targets for no gain during Sunday night's 30-26 loss to Denver.
11586.long: Corum saw nine less carries than backfield mate Kyren Williams in Week 3, the widest discrepancy between the two in a contest so far this season. Corum did get his highest amount of targets in a contest since he logged four targets against the Colts in Week 4 of the 2025 campaign, though he didn't really do much with his two catches Sunday. The running back has now rushed 28 times for 148 yards while catching three of five targets for 13 yards over three games to open the 2026 season.

2133.short: Adams caught seven of 13 targets for 137 yards in Sunday's 30-26 loss to the Broncos.
2133.long: Adams continued to thrive as Matthew Stafford's top target in the absence of Puka Nacua (hip). During Nacua's two-game absence, Adams has compiled 15 catches for a whopping 332 yards and two touchdowns. Adams led the NFL with 14 touchdown receptions during the 2025 regular season and is showing no signs of slowing down at age 33 early in the 2026 campaign. He is poised to maintain a prominent role in Week 4 against the Eagles, though the Rams are optimistic that Nacua could be cleared to return by then.

8150.short: Williams rushed 15 times for 88 yards while catching six of seven targets for 70 yards in Sunday's 30-26 loss to the Broncos.
8150.long: Williams was far more effective than Blake Corum, who turned six carries and four targets into just 15 scrimmage yards. Williams' season-opening touchdown streak came to a halt at two games, but he has been one of the league's top all-around performers at running back in the early going, averaging 5.6 yards per carry while catching 11 of 12 targets and scoring a touchdown apiece as a rusher and a receiver. The Rams are off to a 1-2 start heading into a Week 4 trip to Philadelphia, so expect Los Angeles to continue leaning heavily on its top backfield option in an effort to avoid losing more ground in the NFC standings.

421.short: Stafford completed 30 of 55 passes for 390 yards, two touchdowns and two interceptions in Sunday's 30-26 loss to the Broncos. He also rushed twice for 13 yards.
421.long: Stafford guided the Rams to a 16-0 halftime lead courtesy of a five-yard touchdown pass to Tyler Higbee followed by three Harrison Mevis field goals. LA's lead was erased in the third quarter, and after retaking the lead in the fourth, Stafford threw a disastrous pick-six that Talanoa Hufanga took 66 yards to the house to give the Broncos their first lead with 4:49 remaining. That pick-six was the 33rd Stafford has thrown in his regular-season career, surpassing Brett Favre for sole possession of first place in that dubious stat. Stafford was unfazed by that mistake and responded with a four-play, 77-yard touchdown drive, capped by a 48-yard touchdown pass to Konata Mumpfield, but Hufanga got the last laugh by picking off Stafford in the end zone on the game's final play to seal Denver's 30-26 victory. Stafford has posted gaudy numbers over the last two games despite playing without top wide receiver Puka Nacua (hip), whom the Rams are hoping to get back in Week 4 at Philadelphia.

6865.short: Parkinson (shoulder) has returned to Sunday's game against the Broncos, Stu Jackson of the Rams' official site reports.
6865.long: Parkinson wasn't out of the game long after being deemed questionable to return in the first half. He didn't have a catch prior to the injury but will have a chance to add to his stat line as he plays through this shoulder issue, as well as a knee injury that had Parkinson listed as questionable heading into Sunday night's game.

12487.short: Ferguson (ankle) has returned to Sunday's game against the Broncos, Stu Jackson of the Rams' official site reports.
12487.long: Ferguson had been deemed questionable to return after heading to the locker room in the first quarter. He was taken to the X-ray room, per Cameron DaSilva of USA Today, but Ferguson evidently received good news regarding his ankle injury and has been cleared to resume playing.

11726.short: Kinchens (hamstring) is inactive for Sunday night's contest against Denver, Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com reports.
11726.long: Kinchens will be forced to miss a second straight game after suffering a hamstring injury Week 1 versus San Francisco. In his absence, Josh Wallace will stand to see a larger workload at safety during Sunday Night Football.

13275.short: Simpson (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the Rams' emergency third quarterback for Sunday night's contest against the Broncos, Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com reports.
13275.long: Simpson will operate as the No. 3 QB for the third straight week to open the 2026 campaign. He will only be able to enter the game if both starter Matthew Stafford and top backup Stetson Bennett are forced to exit the contest.

9493.short: Nacua (hip) is inactive for Sunday's game in Denver, Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com reports.
9493.long: Nacua has been listed as a non-participant on each of the Rams' last five injury reports as he deals with a hip injury that head coach Sean McVay has termed "soreness in his groin" that's unrelated to the psoas discomfort that he dealt with in training camp. McVay told Barshop on Friday that if Nacua doesn't suit up Sunday, he likely will be back in action Week 4 at Philadelphia. While Nacua misses a second consecutive contest, fellow WR Davante Adams again will have unfettered access to targets from QB Matthew Stafford, with Jordan Whittington, Konata Mumpfield and Xavier Smith the others available at the position.

3973.short: Garrett (knee) is facing a six-week recovery from surgery on his left knee, but the pass rusher is determined to be back before then, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network and ESPN reports.
3973.long: Garrett required a knee scope after Week 1 and was placed on injured reserve on Sept. 17. He's already missed one game as a result and must sit out at least three more contests while on the list, but Rapoport's report indicates his rehab may extend beyond the Rams' Week 6 road matchup with the Cardinals on Sunday, Oct. 18.

13315.short: The Rams elevated Connors from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday ahead of Sunday's game against the Broncos.
13315.long: With No. 3 running back Ronnie Rivers (calf) moving to IR, Connors will be the primary depth option behind Kyren Williams and Blake Corum for Sunday's contest. Connors, an undrafted free agent out of Houston, will be suiting up for his NFL debut, though it is uncertain if the 23-year-old will receive any snaps or carries in the showdown with the Broncos.

8659.short: Landman (shoulder) does not carry an injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Broncos, Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com reports.
8659.long: Landman tied for a team-high seven tackles in Monday's 28-6 victory over the Giants. He was limited in practice throughout the week because of a shoulder injury, though that doesn't appear to be enough to keep him off the field in Week 3.

11623.short: Whittington (quadriceps) does not carry an injury designation ahead of Sunday's game versus Denver, Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com reports.
11623.long: Whittington wasn't available for Monday's 28-6 win over the Giants. He didn't practice Wednesday to begin the week. However, head coach Sean McVay indicated the wideout would be available in Week 3, so his full participation in Friday's practice and omission from the injury report isn't a surprise. With Puka Nacua (hip) doubtful, Whittington could be in line for a more prominent role alongside Davante Adams.

8195.short: The Rams placed Rivers (calf) on their injured reserve list Wednesday.
8195.long: Per Stu Jackson of the Rams' official site, coach Sean McVay said Wednesday that Rivers' calf injury is expected to keep him sidelined for 4-to-6 weeks. McVay also said the team plans to elevate either undrafted rookie Dean Connors or Jordan Waters from its practice squad for Sunday's game at Denver.

7136.short: Curl recorded four tackles (four solo) and a pass breakup in Monday night's win over the Giants.
7136.long: Curl dealt with an ankle injury during the week but ultimately didn't carry an injury designation into Week 2 against New York. He ended up playing all 58 defensive snaps and now has seven tackles (five solo) and the one pass breakup through two contests to begin the season.

8330.short: Lake recorded seven tackles (six solo), three pass breakups and a forced fumble in Monday night's 28-6 win over the Giants.
8330.long: With the Giants forced to pass much of the night, there were plenty of opportunities to make plays on the ball in the air for the Rams. Lake has now posted back-to-back games of three pass breakups, and he's logged 17 tackles (13 solo) with one interception.

11168.short: Smith did not catch his only target during Monday's 28-6 win versus the Giants, but he recorded four punt returns for 32 yards and two kickoff returns for 29 yards.
11168.long: With usual lead target Puka Nacua (groin) out, Smith was actually the Rams' third option at wide receiver in Week 2 in terms of offensive snaps (25) behind 2025 seventh-rounder Konata Mumpfield (42) and veteran Davante Adams (38), but Adams was the only Rams wideout who saw more than two targets. Smith remained heavily involved on special teams, however, and that will probably continue to be his primary function as long as one of Nacua or Adams is in pads.

13296.short: Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley said Douglas (ankle) is day-to-day and could practice Wednesday, Travis Wingfield of the team's official site reports.
13296.long: Douglas was inactive for Sunday's 24-10 loss to the Chiefs due to the ankle injury, but the Dolphins are seemingly optimistic that his absence won't extend beyond that. The rookie wideout has carved out a notable role right off the bat for Miami, logging snap shares north of 85 percent in both of the team's first two games while producing a 7-113-0 receiving line on 10 targets.

11643.short: Head coach Jeff Hafley said Monday that he considers Wright (stinger/foot) to be "day-to-day," Joe Schad of The Palm Beach Post reports.
11643.long: Wright's health is notable considering the Dolphins lost No. 1 RB De'Von Achane to a torn ACL during Sunday's loss to the Chiefs. Having said that, Hafley also called Wright "day-to-day" last Monday after he emerged from Week 2 at San Francisco with a stinger and foot injury, which didn't allow him to play Week 3. Wright likely will need to get through this week without a DNP to put himself in the running to help cover for the absent Achane. Currently, Ollie Gordon is the only healthy RB on Miami's active roster.

9226.short: Achane (knee) was diagnosed Monday with a torn ACL and will miss the remainder of the season, Ian Rapoport and Adam Schefter of ESPN report.
9226.long: After Achane was forced out early in Sunday's 24-10 loss to the Chiefs, Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley acknowledged that he wasn't optimistic about the initial evaluations of the running back's injury. Follow-up testing Monday confirmed the Dolphins' worst fears, as the team's top playmaker will now be headed for season-ending surgery. Assuming he experiences no setbacks during what will be a lengthy rehab process, Achane could be ready to go for Week 1 of the 2027 campaign, but the Dolphins will now be left with Jaylen Wright (foot/stinger) and Ollie Gordon as their main backfield options for the final 14 games of 2026.

8161.short: Willis completed 20 of 36 passes for 210 yards, no touchdowns and one interception in Sunday's 24-10 loss to the Chiefs. He also rushed nine times for 56 yards and lost a fumble.
8161.long: Willis led the team in rushing yards in a game starting running back De'Von Achane (knee) left in the first quarter. Achane could be facing a lengthy absence, which would further deplete a Dolphins offense that already lacks playmakers and entered Sunday's loss without wide receiver Caleb Douglas (ankle) and backup running back Jaylen Wright (foot). Willis has yet to exceed 220 passing yards or produce a multi-touchdown performance for the Dolphins, though he has rushed for at least 39 yards twice in three games ahead of a Week 4 road game at Minnesota.

12495.short: Gordon rushed 17 times for 41 yards and a touchdown while catching all three of his targets for 14 yards in Sunday's 24-10 loss to the Chiefs.
12495.long: Gordon capitalized on his added opportunities after De'Von Achane (knee) exited the game in the first quarter. The 2025 sixth-round pick capped Miami's 17-play, 91-yard opening drive with a three-yard touchdown run, one play after Gordon converted a third-and-9 with an 11-yard run. Miami's offense produced just three points the rest of the way and Gordon exited briefly due to cramps but returned. Achane is feared to have a major injury, and if Jaylen Wright (foot) is also unable to play against the Vikings in Week 3, Gordon would be in line to handle a substantial workload again in the Dolphins' struggling offense.

11421.short: Miller (hip/back) is active for Sunday's game against the Chiefs.
11421.long: Miller was questionable ahead of the meeting with Kansas City due to hip and back injuries. However, the wideout is good to go. With Caleb Douglas (ankle) ruled out, Miller, who had a touchdown in Week 2 against the 49ers, could be more involved.

13311.short: Bell (knee) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Chiefs.
13311.long: With fellow rookie wideout Caleb Douglas (ankle) ruled out, Bell will take on a larger role in Miami's passing game despite recently dealing with fluid buildup and soreness in his surgically repaired right knee. Doctors told him it isn't a major concern, and Bell then told reporters Thursday that he plans to play Week 3.

11663.short: Robinson has cleared the concussion protocol and is available to play in Sunday's matchup with the Chiefs, Marcel Louis-Jacques of ESPN.com reports.
11663.long: The defensive end likely suffered the concussion in Week 1 against the Raiders and then missed the Dolphins' Week 2 clash with the 49ers. Robinson has suffered three concussions in the last two seasons and told reporters he would wear the Guardian Cap on his helmet this week versus Kansas City, per Joe Schad of The Palm Beach Post. The Miami Herald's Barry Jackson reported that Robinson has suffered "at least" five concussions in this three-year NFL career.

13338.short: Coleman played 27 offensive snaps and saw no targets in Sunday's 35-13 loss to the 49ers.
13338.long: Coleman played 46 percent of the Dolphins' offensive snaps in the blowout loss. The fifth-round rookie appears to have taken a back seat to Malik Washington, Caleb Douglas (ankle) and Chris Bell. Coleman could see an uptick in usage in the team's Week 3 game against the Chiefs if Douglas cannot play due to his ankle injury.

6949.short: Brooks recorded three total tackles (two solo) during Sunday's 35-13 loss to San Francisco.
6949.long: Brooks uncharastically quiet, registering his fewest tackles in a game since Week 17 of the 2024 campaign. The linebacker notched a career-high 183 total tackles over 17 regular-season games in 2025, and he'll likely be more busy Week 3 versus the Chiefs.

13453.short: Rodriguez recorded eight total tackles (three solo) during Sunday's 35-13 loss to the 49ers.
13453.long: Rodriguez finished second on the team in takedowns behind safety Michael Taaffe (nine). The rookie linebacker has now registered 22 total tackles (eight solo) over the first two games of his NFL career.

11610.short: Washington caught four of his five targets for 43 yards, rushed once for four yards, returned a punt for seven yards and returned three kickoffs for 69 yards in Sunday's 35-13 loss to the 49ers.
11610.long: Washington played 43 of the Dolphins' 59 offensive snaps as well as six special-teams snaps. The No. 1 wide receiver and returner's name appeared across the box score, and Washington appears set to continue filling a diverse role on a rebuilding Miami squad.

8172.short: Dulcich caught two of his three targets for 17 yards in Sunday's 35-13 loss to the 49ers.
8172.long: Dulcich had a larger role on offense after a quiet opener against the Raiders. The tight end played 36 of 59 offensive snaps Sunday and garnered a bit more attention downfield. Dulcich also contributed on special teams, playing four snaps in the loss.

7922.short: Patterson converted two of his three field-goal attempts and his sole extra-point try during the Dolphins' 35-13 loss to the 49ers.
7922.long: Patterson appears to be achieving the wrong kind of consistency. The kicker once again converted 67 percent of his field-goal attempts, missing one of his three kicks, as he did in the Dolphins' Week 1 loss to the Raiders. Patterson moves to 4-for-6 on field-goal attempts and 2-for-2 on PATs through two games.

5025.short: The Dolphins placed Harrison (hamstring) on injured reserve Saturday.
5025.long: Harrison was ruled out ahead of Sunday's game against the 49ers due to his injury. The linebacker suffered the hamstring injury during the Dolphins' Week 1 loss to the Raiders and has been unable to practice since the incident. Harrison will now need to miss at least four games on IR before becoming eligible to return to the active roster.

5973.short: Oliver was diagnosed with a torn biceps following an MRI on Monday and is expected to undergo surgery in the coming days, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com reports.
5973.long: According to Fowler, Oliver is a long shot to make a full recovery from surgery before the end of the regular season, though the tight end may have an outside chance at being available in the playoffs, should the Vikings qualify. A key blocker for the Vikings, Oliver had taken the field for 56.9 percent of the team's offensive snaps through the first three games and recorded three receptions for 46 yards on five targets.

11792.short: Reichard hit all three field-goal attempts and both extra-point tries in Sunday's 23-16 win over the Bucs.
11792.long: The kicker made field goals from 56, 54 and 43 yards, respectively. Reichard has yet to miss in 2026, and he has now connected on four field-goal tries from 50 yards or longer.

9756.short: Addison hauled in five of nine targets for 90 yards and one touchdown during Sunday's 23-16 victory at Tampa Bay.
9756.long: Serving as the Vikings' de facto No. 1 wide receiver after Justin Jefferson (ankle) exited in the first half and didn't return, Addison parlayed the opportunity into his most productive performance of the young campaign. In particular, Addison connected with QB Kyler Murray for a 41-yard TD (his first of the season) with less than five minutes left in the second quarter. Head coach Kevin O'Connell told Ben Goessling of The Minnesota Star Tribune afterward that Minnesota isn't too worried about Jefferson's health concern, so even if he's able to suit up next Sunday versus the Dolphins, Addison could hold more sway in the offense if Jefferson isn't 100 percent.

4199.short: Jones tallied 17 carries for 58 yards and reeled in five of six targets for 34 yards during Sunday's 23-16 win in Tampa Bay.
4199.long: After dealing with a knee injury during Week 3 prep, Jones continued to lead the Vikings backfield Sunday with Jordan Mason (thumb) on injured reserve. With the help of his first catches of the season, Jones surpassed 20 touches for a second game in a row, a span in which he's turned 45 touches into 197 yards from scrimmage. Meanwhile, reserve RBs DeeJay Dallas and Demond Claiborne combined for four touches this weekend. Jones may operate with some practice restrictions during Week 4 prep but should remain Minnesota's No. 1 back next Sunday against the Dolphins, assuming he again is available.

5849.short: Murray (concussion) completed 15 of 29 passes for 168 yards, one touchdown and one interception and took two carries for 17 yards during Sunday's 23-16 win at Tampa Bay.
5849.long: In his first game action since suffering a concussion in the first quarter of a Week 1 victory against the Packers, Murray lost No. 1 WR Justin Jefferson (ankle) in the first half Sunday but largely avoided any game-changing mistakes while leading the Vikings to a 3-0 record on the season. Murray's first TD pass with Minnesota was a 41-yard connection with Jordan Addison late in the second quarter, while his pick well inside Vikings territory in the middle of the third quarter resulted in only a made Chase McLaughlin field-goal attempt for Tampa Bay. Murray's next chance for game action is next Sunday versus the Dolphins.

6794.short: Jefferson (ankle) "got close a couple times" to returning to Sunday's 23-16 win over the Buccaneers, head coach Kevin O'Connell said after the game, Ben Goessling of the Minnesota Star Tribune reports.
6794.long: Jefferson sustained an ankle injury in the first half and ultimately was ruled out for the remainder of the game after catching both of his early targets for 32 yards. The Vikings held on without their star receiver to improve to 3-0 heading into a Week 4 home game against the Dolphins. Jefferson's ankle injury will be evaluated further, but O'Connell sounded optimistic that Jefferson may not face much, if any, additional missed time.

13513.short: Demmings (hamstring) has been ruled out for the remainder of Sunday's contest against the Buccaneers.
13513.long: Demmings suffered a hamstring injury in the third quarter, and his day has now officially come to a premature end. In his absence, the Vikings have become rather thin in the secondary.

11086.short: Pace (personal) is active for Sunday's game against the Buccaneers.
11086.long: Pace popped up on Saturday's injury report as questionable due to a personal matter, but he's been cleared to play in Sunday's road game. He has six tackles (three solo) through the first two games of the regular season.

6931.short: Dallas (toe) practiced fully Friday and doesn't have a designation for Sunday's game in Tampa Bay.
6931.long: Dallas kicked off Week 3 prep with back-to-back limited sessions due to a toe injury, but his ability to handle every on-field rep Friday clears him to be available to the Vikings backfield this weekend. With Aaron Jones (knee) also gaining clearance to play Sunday, Dallas likely will remain relegated to a small workload, as the latter has just four touches on his 14 offensive snaps through two games on the campaign.

12683.short: Ingram-Dawkins (oblique) was a full participant in Thursday's practice.
12683.long: Ingram-Dawkins was limited Wednesday to begin the practice week, though after being upgraded Thursday, it seems as if he will be good to go Sunday versus Tampa Bay. The 23-year-old finished his rookie campaign in 2025 with 12 total tackles (six solo), including 1.0 sacks, and one pass defended.

7049.short: Jennings (personal) was not listed on the Vikings' injury report Wednesday.
7049.long: Jennings was unable to practice all week before ultimately sitting out Sunday's 9-3 win over the Bears while dealing with a personal matter. The 29-year-old returned to practice Wednesday, and he'll stand to operate as Minnesota's No. 3 option at wide receiver in the return of quarterback Kyler Murray against the Buccaneers in Week 3.

5864.short: Murphy tallied seven tackles (four solo) and an interception during Sunday's win over the Bears.
5864.long: Murphy had a strong outing, as he picked off Caleb Williams (hamstring) to force one of the team's two turnovers. Murphy also finished second on the team in tackles, bringing his total on the season 15 (11 solo) across just two games.

6217.short: Cashman logged 10 tackles (six solo), including 1.0 sacks, during Sunday's win over the Bears.
6217.long: Cashman had a dominant outing during the victory, leading Chicago in tackles while recording one of the team's four sacks. The 30-year-old has gotten off to a strong start this season, racking up 17 tackles (11 solo), including 1.5 sacks, across his first two outings, and he'll look to keep producing in Week 3 versus the Buccaneers.

13347.short: Claiborne caught his sole target for two yards in Sunday's 9-3 win over the Bears.
13347.long: Claiborne is the No. 2 running back behind Aaron Jones while Jordan Mason (thumb) recovers on IR. The 22-year-old saw just two offensive snaps in Sunday's game, meaning DeeJay Dallas could have a shot at claiming the backup role from the sixth-rounder in the future.

11667.short: Turner logged five tackles (three solo), including 2.0 sacks, during the Vikings' 9-3 win over the Bears on Sunday.
11667.long: Turner opened the season with a sack against the Packers in Week 1, and he doubled his output during Sunday's NFC North showdown. Both of his sacks came in the second half, with the second a nine-yard takedown of Tyson Bagent on the final play of the game to seal the win for Minnesota. Per Sheil Kapadia of The Athletic, Turner leads the league with 20 pressures through two regular-season games, and his 3.0 sacks are tied for third-most behind Greg Rousseau (4.0) and T.J. Watt (3.5). Up next is a Week 3 road clash against the Buccaneers and quarterback Baker Mayfield, who has been sacked seven times through two games to open the 2026 campaign.

5859.short: Brown was spotted Monday in the Patriots' locker room walking without a limp and wearing a small wrap on his injured right ankle, Taylor Kyles of CLNSMedia.com reports.
5859.long: Kyles noted that Brown was wearing cleats, which could hint that he was able to do some on-field exercises. After being placed on injured reserve Sept. 12, Brown won't be eligible to start practicing with his teammates until Week 6, but the wideout at least seems to be making good progress in his recovery from the high-ankle sprain he sustained in the season-opening loss to the Seahawks.

4177.short: Hollins caught six of nine targets for 87 yards during Sunday's 35-6 loss to the Jaguars.
4177.long: Hollins saw nearly twice as many targets as the next closest option DeMario Douglas (five), and his 87 yards were his highest total in a regular-season contest since Week 10 of the 2025 campaign. With A.J. Brown (ankle) on injured reserve, someone will have to take the reins as the Patriots' top option at wide receiver, and Hollins certainly showed he's capable of handling a larger workload.

7611.short: Stevenson rushed seven times for 22 yards and brought in all three targets for 16 yards in the Patriots' 35-6 loss to the Jaguars on Sunday.
7611.long: As was the case with backfield mate TreVeyon Henderson, Stevenson saw his opportunities on the ground capped to an extent by a game script that saw the Patriots already down 11 by halftime and 25 heading into the fourth quarter. Stevenson was just one carry and rushing yard apiece behind Henderson's workload on the ground, and both backs will look to be more involved in a key Week 4 road matchup against the Bills next Sunday.

12529.short: Henderson rushed eight times for 23 yards and brought in his only target for six yards in the Patriots' 35-6 loss to the Jaguars on Sunday.
12529.long: Playing in his second game of the season, Henderson led the Patriots in carries and rushing yards, yet each of those figures were only one more than those generated by backfield mate Rhamondre Stevenson. Henderson had a much more efficient showing in his Week 2 season debut with a 16-carry, 76-yard, one-touchdown showing against the Steelers, but game script had a significant impact on the volume for both of the Patriots' backs Sunday. Henderson will look to get back on track in a key Week 4 road divisional matchup against the Bills next Sunday.

11564.short: Maye completed 14 of 25 passes for 199 yards with no touchdowns and two interceptions and added four carries for 18 yards in the Patriots' 35-6 loss to the Jaguars on Sunday. He also committed two fumbles, losing one.
11564.long: Maye's rough afternoon also included three sacks, and the multi-interception tally was already his second of the first three games of the new season. The 2024 first-round pick was able to lead his team to only two field goals, and two of his three turnovers were followed by Jaguars touchdowns on the ensuing drive. It's clear Maye misses No. 1 target A.J. Brown (ankle, IR), and although the latter's absence wasn't anywhere near as impactful in a Week 2 win over the Steelers where the defense held Pittsburgh to three points, it was glaring in a game where New England needed to consistently score points. Brown still is slated to miss several more games, and Maye will have plenty of pressure on him in a Week 4 road matchup against Josh Allen and the Bills.

7664.short: Barmore (shoulder) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against Jacksonville.
7664.long: If Barmore can't return to the Week 3 meeting versus the Jaguars, it could mean more work for Joshua Farmer and Jeremiah Pharms.

12710.short: Reed is expected to start alongside Kevin Byard at safety against the Jaguars on Sunday, Evan Lazar of the Patriots' official site reports.
12710.long: Craig Woodson (shoulder) is inactive, so Reed will draw his first start of the season. Reed saw some playing time on defense during the Patriots' Week 2 win over the Steelers, with the second-year pro finishing with two tackles (one solo).

13573.short: Hutchins (knee) was placed on injured reserve Friday.
13573.long: Hutchins appeared in both of the Patriots' first two games of the 2026 campaign, accumulating three total tackles. The rookie will now miss at least four games while tending to a knee injury. While Hutchins has played sparingly, his absence will still allow Gabe Jacas and Jose Ramirez to see a little more action.

7204.short: Gilliam (knee) does not have any injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Jaguars.
7204.long: Gilliam was limited in all three Week 3 practice sessions. The fullback sustained a knee injury during the Patriots' Week 2 win over the Steelers, but it won't stop the 29-year-old from suiting up for Sunday's game against the Jaguars. Gilliam has seen 33 offensive snaps and 26 special-teams snaps through two games in 2026.

12115.short: The Patriots placed Pettus (ankle) on injured reserve Wednesday.
12115.long: Pettus exited the second quarter of Sunday's 20-3 win over the Steelers with an ankle injury, and he'll now have to miss at least the next four games while on IR. With Craig Woodson (shoulder) also injured, the team will likely look to sign or elevate a player from the practice squad  for Sunday's Week 3 matchup against the Jaguars.

8726.short: The Patriots opened the 21-day practice window for Schooler (back) on Wednesday.
8726.long: Schooler can now return to practice but won't be eligible to appear in a game until Week 5 due to being on the reserve/non-football injury list. Once officially activated, the 29-year-old should contribute as a depth defender.

5054.short: Davis (neck) was a full participant at practice Wednesday.
5054.long: Davis was unavailable for the team's Week 2 win over the Steelers as a result of a neck injury, but he now appears to be healthy ahead of Sunday's contest against the Jaguars. The 29-year-old will slot in as a starting cornerback versus Jacksonville.

12547.short: Williams caught one of two targets for 10 yards in Sunday's 20-3 win over the Steelers.
12547.long: Despite A.J. Brown (ankle) missing his first game after going down in Week 1 against Seattle, Williams played just 20 percent of the Patriots' offensive snaps against Pittsburgh. He operated as the fourth receiver, well behind Mack Hollins, Romeo Doubs and slot man DeMario Douglas. Williams doesn't hold much fantasy value in redraft formats.

5726.short: Spillane logged six tackles (three solo) in Sunday's 20-3 win over the Steelers.
5726.long: Spillane played 100 percent of the Patriots' 70 defensive snaps in Sunday's contest. The inside linebacker has now played all 120 of the team's defensive snaps through two regular-season games.

12137.short: Woods logged 10 tackles (eight solo) and defensed one pass in Sunday's 20-3 win over the Steelers.
12137.long: Woods played 86 percent of the Patriots' defensive snaps in Sunday's contest. The cornerback started in place of Carlton Davis (neck), and he'll likely do so again in Week 3 against the Jaguars if the latter remains absent.

12978.short: Ponder logged five tackles (three solo), including 1.0 sacks, and recovered a fumble he returned for a touchdown in Sunday's 20-3 win over the Steelers.
12978.long: Ponder recovered an Aaron Rodgers fumble and took it 19 yards for a touchdown to extend the Patriots' 13-3 lead to the game-winning 20-3 score. The outside linebacker played 77 percent of the team's defensive snaps in the contest.

7921.short: Elliss logged 12 tackles (seven solo), including 1.0 sacks, and forced a fumble in Sunday's 20-3 win over the Steelers.
7921.long: Elliss led all players in Sunday's contest in tackles. The inside linebacker played all 70 defensive snaps in the contest and has missed just one defensive snap through two regular-season games.

7543.short: Saints head coach Kellen Moore said that Etienne will have some "time lost" due to the hamstring injury he sustained in Sunday's 35-27 loss to the Raiders, Mike Triplett of NewOrleans.Football reports.
7543.long: Moore noted that a specific timeline for Etienne's return hasn't been established, making it uncertain whether or not the running back will be able to avoid a stint on injured reserve. At the very least, Etienne will be sidelined for the Saints' Week 4 game against the Falcons next Monday, which likely paves the way for Alvin Kamara to take on an expanded profile in the backfield after working in a complementary role the previous two weeks. Reserve backs Kendre Miller and CJ Donaldson should also be in store for more opportunities for however long Etienne is out.

5857.short: Fant caught all four of his targets for 33 yards and two touchdowns during Sunday's 35-27 loss to Las Vegas.
5857.long: Fant made the most of his opportunities, connecting with quarterback Tyler Shough for a three-yard touchdown in the second quarter and a 16-yard score in the third quarter. The tight end is the No. 2 option behind Juwan Johnson at his position, but Fant has still caught eight of 12 targets for 66 yards and three scores over the first three games this year.

7002.short: Johnson caught all eight of his targets for 53 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 35-27 loss to the Raiders.
7002.long: The veteran tight end continues to have an impressive start to the season, hauling in TD strikes of one and two yards from Tyler Shough. but Johnson had a tough end to his day as he fumbled to end the Saints' final possession while they were trying to mount a comeback late in the fourth quarter. Johnson has put together a 15-173-3 line on 19 targets through three games, and he'll look to atone for his miscue in a Week 4 home tilt against the Falcons.

4035.short: Kamara carried the ball nine times for 36 yards and caught his only target for five yards in Sunday's 35-27 loss to the Raiders.
4035.long: The veteran RB once again took a back seat to Travis Etienne to begin the game, but that changed after the former Jaguar aggravated a hamstring strain and left the game in the third quarter. Over the Saints' last five possessions, Kamara split the workload in the backfield with Kendre Miller, getting six touches to Miller's five. The severity of Etienne's injury isn't yet clear, but if he misses significant time, Kamara and Miller would likely continue working in tandem, with rookie CJ Donaldson also potentially mixing in as a short-yardage option.

12545.short: Shough completed 29 of 42 passes for 255 yards and four touchdowns with one interception in Sunday's 35-27 loss to the Raiders. He added 36 rushing yards on his lone carry but also lost two fumbles.
12545.long: The second-year QB was dynamic once again, tossing two TDs each to tight ends Juwan Johnson and Noah Fant, but protection issues in the absence of left tackle Kelvin Banks (ankle) ending up proving costly as all four of the Saints' fourth-quarter possessions ended in turnovers, causing them to squander a 27-22 lead. Shough has thrown eight touchdowns through three games but has also given the ball away six times (three INTs and three lost fumbles), and he'll try to clean up those issues in Week 4 at home against the Falcons.

8144.short: Olave caught nine of 13 targets for 107 yards in Sunday's 35-27 loss to the Raiders.
8144.long: The fifth-year wideout led the Saints in catches, targets and receiving yards, but all four of Tyler Shough's TD passes went to tight ends instead of Olave. Olave has hauled in more than 100 yards in two of three games to begin the season, amassing a 27-375-1 line on 36 targets, and he'll look to keep rolling in Week 4 at home against the Falcons.

6848.short: Jennings has a knee injury and is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Raiders.
6848.long: The linebacker recorded three tackles (two solo) and a pass breakup before exiting. Jennings played more on special teams than defense in New Orleans' first two games.

5912.short: Granderson (ankle) has returned to Sunday's contest against the Raiders, Ross Jackson of WWL Louisiana reports.
5912.long: Granderson was briefly sidelined with an ankle injury that he suffered in the third quarter, but he has now returned to action. The 29-year-old is back in his starting role as a weak-side linebacker for New Orleans.

7647.short: Werner (neck) is questionable to return to Sunday's contest against the Raiders, Matthew Paras of The New Orleans Times-Picayune reports.
7647.long: Werner suffered a stinger in the first half, and his status for the rest of the game is now in question. In his absence, Isaiah Stalbird and Danny Stutsman are two candidates to see an increase in workload at inside linebacker.

8390.short: Emerson (shoulder) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Raiders.
8390.long: Emerson injured his shoulder during the Saints' Week 2 win over the Ravens. He drew the questionable tag for Week 3 following a limited practice Friday, but he'll be sidelined for Sunday's game after failing to be cleared by medical staff following pregame warmups. Jayden Price, Michael Reid and Decamerion Richardson will provide depth in the secondary in Emerson's absence.

7538.short: Wilson (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the emergency third quarterback against the Raiders on Sunday.
7538.long: For a third consecutive week, Wilson will be the Saints' emergency QB3, meaning he cannot play Sunday unless both Tyler Shough and Spencer Rattler leave the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

11506.short: The Saints elevated Moreno-Cropper from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday ahead of Sunday's game against the Raiders.
11506.long: Moreno-Cropper is set for his first taste of regular-season action in 2026. The wide receiver is being elevated alongside Kevin Austin to supplement a Saints wide receiver corps now without Barion Brown (hamstring). With Week 3 marking Austin's third practice squad elevation, the Saints will be unable to utilize him in the future without signing him to the active roster. This predicament means Moreno-Cropper may be the go-to wide receiver elevation for Week 4 and Week 5 if the team likes his game-day performance in Week 3.

8200.short: The Saints elevated Austin from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday ahead of Sunday's game against the Raiders.
8200.long: Austin has been elevated for a third consecutive week, meaning the Saints have elected to exhaust the wide receiver's final practice squad elevation just three weeks into the 2026 regular season. Austin has logged 10 offensive snaps and five special-teams snaps over his two contests, catching his only target for seven yards.

9757.short: Miller (illness) doesn't carry an injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Raiders.
9757.long: Miller was under the weather Thursday, keeping him off the practice field. However, he was a full participant Friday. Miller was a healthy scratch for the 24-17 win over Baltimore in Week 2, meaning he is in danger of suffering the same fate versus Las Vegas, though his services may be needed on special teams with WR Barion Brown (hamstring) ruled out. With that in mind, if Miller is inactive, that would likely mean more work for Alvin Kamara and CJ Donaldson behind Travis Etienne.

12619.short: Sanker (knee) was a full participant in Thursday's practice, Mike Triplett of NewOrleans.Football reports.
12619.long: Sanker had limited practice participation Wednesday seemingly as a precautionary measure, and his return to a full session Thursday puts the second-year defensive back on track to play Sunday against Las Vegas. Sanker has 13 tackles (10 solo) through two regular-season games.

6782.short: Young (calf) was a full participant in Thursday's practice, Mike Triplett of NewOrleans.Football reports.
6782.long: Young opened Week 3 prep as a limited participant in Wednesday's practice due to a calf injury, but his full session Thursday puts the seventh-year pass rusher on track to play against the Raiders on Sunday. Young has two tackles (one solo), including 1.5 sacks, and one pass defense through the first two games of the regular season.

11893.short: Stalbird (shoulder) was a full participant at the Saints' practice Wednesday.
11893.long: Stalbird was unavailable for the team's 24-17 win over the Ravens in Week 2 due to a shoulder injury, but he now appears to be back to full health. The 26-year-old will be back in his role as a top depth option behind Kaden Elliss and Pete Werner at inside linebacker Sunday versus the Raiders.

13319.short: Delp gathered in his only target for eight yards during Sunday's 24-17 victory over the Ravens.
13319.long: Delp didn't suit up for the 31-30 overtime loss to Detroit in Week 1 due to a hamstring issue, though he was on the field for Sunday's 24-17 upset win over Baltimore. However, despite the rookie's availability in Week 2, he appeared in just nine of the Saints' 68 offensive snaps, catching his only target for eight yards, while logging six snaps on special teams. Although Delp could see more action moving ahead, it doesn't appear as if he will be more involved than Noah Fant and Juwan Johnson anytime soon.

11565.short: The Giants acquired McCarthy from the Vikings on Monday in exchange for a 2027 fifth-round pick, Tom Pelissero of Netflix reports.
11565.long: The No. 10 overall pick in the 2024 NFL Draft, McCarthy had fallen out of favor in Minnesota and had dropped behind both Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz on the depth chart. The 23-year-old will get a fresh opportunity in New York, where he should at least settle in as the No. 2 quarterback behind Jameis Winston while Jaxson Dart (knee) is likely out for the season. Though Winston led the Giants to a 12-7 win over the Titans in his first start this past Sunday, he's completed just 25 of 49 pass attempts for 229 yards (4.7 YPA) while playing nearly two full games. Another underwhelming performance or two from Winston could compel the Giants to give McCarthy a look in the starting role once he has time to get up to speed with the new playbook.

5862.short: The Giants fear that Burns sustained a torn ACL in his right knee during Sunday's 12-7 win over the Titans, Jeff Howe and Jonathan Jones of The Athletic report.
5862.long: New York will hope that an MRI on Monday yields better news for Burns, but the team is bracing for the possibility of the star pass rusher missing the rest of the season. Burns had been held without a sack through the Giants' first three games, but he led the NFC with 16.5 during the 2025 campaign. If Burns ends up missing any length of time, Kayvon Thibodeaux would likely move into a full-time role on the edge opposite Abdul Carter.

13833.short: Zvada made all four of his field-goal attempts during the Giants' 12-7 win over the Titans on Sunday.
13833.long: Neither team could generate that much offense in tough conditions Sunday, but Zvada helped the Giants build and maintain their lead with four field goals, all of which came from within 40 yards. The rookie kicker has made all six of his field-goal attempts and each of his four extra-point tries through the first three games of the regular season.

2306.short: Winston completed 14 of 22 passes for 118 yards in Sunday's 12-7 win over Tennessee. He added 14 rushing yards on two carries.
2306.long: The 32-year-old quarterback was getting his first start in place of Jaxson Dart (knee), but Winston wasn't asked to do very much as the Giants leaned on their backfield and their defense. To his credit, Winston did avoid turnovers, which may be all coach John Harbaugh needs from him. Winston will look for opportunities to be more productive at home in Week 4 against the Cardinals.

11632.short: Nabers caught five of six targets for 26 yards in Sunday's 12-7 win over the Titans.
11632.long: The Giants' passing game struggled with Jameis Winston under center instead of Jaxson Dart (knee), and while Nabers led the team in catches and targets, he didn't make much of an impact -- his longest gain went for just 12 yards. That doesn't bode well for the rest of the third-year wideout's campaign with Dart not expected back until 2027, but Nabers and Winston will have plenty of time to develop more chemistry. Nabers will take a 12-96-0 line on 19 targets into a Week 4 home tilt against the Cardinals.

12481.short: Skattebo carried the ball 20 times for 60 yards and caught three of four targets for 40 yards in Sunday's 12-7 win over the Titans.
12481.long: With Jameis Winston under center instead of Jaxson Dart (knee), the Giants leaned a little more heavily on their backfield and Skattebo saw a season high in touches while hitting for 100-plus scrimmage yards for the first time in 2026. The second-year back's longest play came on a 30-yard toss in the first quarter, as he made himself available downfield to bail out a scrambling Winston. Through three games, Skattebo is showing no ill effects from the ankle injury that ended his rookie campaign early, and he's collected 177 rushing yards and a TD on 50 carries while adding a 7-59-0 line on eight targets. He figures to see a big workload again in Week 4 at home against the Cardinals.

7970.short: With Tyler Nubin (calf) inactive, Washington will start at safety against the Titans on Sunday, Jordan Raanan of ESPN.com reports.
7970.long: Nubin was not cleared by medical staff to play Sunday, so Washington and Jevon Holland will be the Giants' starting safeties for Week 3, with Jason Pinnock and Elijah Campbell providing depth at the position. Washington has two tackles (one solo) through two regular-season games, and the last time he was a regular starter on defense was during the second half of the 2024 campaign as a member of the Ravens.

5121.short: The Giants elevated Berrios from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday ahead of Sunday's game against the Titans, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports.
5121.long: The Giants have elected to expend Berrios' last practice squad elevation, calling upon the wide receiver for three consecutive weeks. The 30-year-old remains the team's primary kick and punt returner, receiving no targets but recording 81 kick-return yards over the past two games. Berrios will need to be signed to the active roster to participate in any more regular-season games for the Giants after Week 3.

10215.short: The Giants signed Haener from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday, Dan Salomone of the team's official site reports.
10215.long: In the wake of Jaxson Dart's serious left knee injury that will sideline him for the rest of the regular season, Jameis Winston will get the first chance to be New York's starting QB on Sunday against the Titans, and Haener's standing as the only other signal-caller on the roster implied that he'd serve as the backup in the initial contest without Dart. Whether or not that'll last beyond Week 3 remains to be seen, but Haener does have NFL experience under his belt, as he completed 18 of 39 passes for 226 yards, one touchdown and one interception and rushed 11 times for 22 yards in eight appearances (one start) as a member of the Saints in 2024.

12508.short: The Giants officially placed Dart (knee) on injured reserve Thursday, Mike Garafolo of NFL Network reports.
12508.long: This transaction was inevitable after it was revealed Dart will miss the rest of the regular season due to damage to the MCL, PCL and meniscus that he suffered in his left knee during the Giants' Week 2 loss to the Rams. Fortunately for Dart, his ACL is intact, and head coach John Harbaugh also told Connor Hughes of SNY.tv on Wednesday that the second-year quarterback may be able to return in the postseason, if the team qualifies. In the meantime, Jameis Winston will cover QB duties for the Giants.

8396.short: McFadden (neck) was listed as a full participant in Wednesday's practice estimate,  Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports.
8396.long: McFadden missed the Giants' Week 2 loss to the Rams due to a neck injury. The linebacker was not able to log more than a limited practice session during Week 2 prep, a benchmark McFadden has already surpassed with his estimate of full participation Wednesday. Absent any setbacks, the 26-year-old should be healthy enough to suit up for Sunday's game against the Titans.

4968.short: Edmunds logged five assisted tackles and one pass defensed in Monday's 28-6 loss to the Rams.
4968.long: Edmunds did not record a solo tackle in Sunday's contest but assisted on five takedowns. The linebacker played 100 percent of the Giants' defensive snaps for the second consecutive week, now having been on the field for all 118 defensive plays this season.

7666.short: Holland logged eight tackles (five solo), one pass defensed for an interception and one fumble recovery in Monday's 28-6 loss to the Rams.
7666.long: Holland tied Tyler Nubin for the most Giants tackles in Monday's loss. The free safety picked off reigning MVP Matthew Stafford in the second quarter of the game as the Giants tried to mount a comeback. Holland also helped force and recovered a Kyren Williams fumble at the Rams' 11-yard line late in the first half, setting up the first of two field goals that constituted New York's scoring Monday night.

11597.short: Johnson played 16 of the Giants' 58 offensive snaps but did not haul in any of his four targets during Monday's 28-6 loss to the Rams.
11597.long: All four of Johnson's targets came in the first half, three of which were in the opening quarter. The third-year tight end failed to record a catch, but he did log a tackle on Trent McDuffie after the latter intercepted Jameis Winston midway through the second quarter. Johnson is firmly behind Isaiah Likely on the depth chart, though all of the Giants pass catchers figure to see their production dip with Winston under center instead of Jaxson Dart, the latter of whom could miss the rest of the season due to a knee injury.

2078.short: Beckham played three of the Giants' 58 offensive snaps and did not see a target in Monday's 28-6 loss to the Rams.
2078.long: Beckham has logged only 14 snaps on offense without recording a target through the first two games of the regular season. Despite the lack of usage, the veteran wide receiver could factor more into the Giants' gameplan moving forward if Malik Nabers were to miss time due to a shoulder injury that he sustained during Monday's loss. The Giants will head back MetLife Stadium to host the Titans on Sunday.

7090.short: Mooney caught two of three targets for 48 yards in Monday night's 28-6 loss to the Rams.
7090.long: Mooney led the team with 48 receiving yards in what was a disappointing outing for New York's offense. Starting quarterback Jaxson Dart suffered a knee injury on the first possession of the game, and he is expected to be sidelined for the foreseeable future. Mooney will look to continue to build chemistry with new starter Jameis Winston in Week 3 against the Titans.

8155.short: Hall is considered week-to-week after an MRI on Monday revealed that his thigh injury isn't significant as feared, Ian Rapoport and Adam Schefter of ESPN report.
8155.long: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn shed more light on the severity of Hall's injury when he speaks to the media Wednesday, but the running back seemingly avoided any sort of a major damage to his thigh that would result in an extended stint on injured reserve. However, with Hall being classified as week-to-week, he may be facing an uphill battle to make it back for the Jets' next game Sunday at Chicago. After Hall exited in the fourth quarter of this past Sunday's 31-24 loss to the Lions, Braelon Allen handled six touches over the Jets' final two possessions. Allen and Isaiah Davis would both be in store for expanded roles if Hall ends up missing any time.

13330.short: Sadiq caught seven of eight passes for 105 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 31-24 loss to the Lions.
13330.long: The rookie tight end made a spectacular play to haul in his first career TD reception in the second quarter, leaping from about the five-yard line and stretching out the full length of his 6-foot-3 frame to bring in a 24-yard pass from Geno Smith. Sadiq is very quickly making an impact with his athleticism, and through his first three NFL games he's compiled a 12-143-1 line on 14 targets while adding a three-yard score on his only carry. He'll look to continue building chemistry with Smith in a Week 4 road trip to Chicago.

1373.short: Smith completed 31 of 37 passes for 321 yards and three touchdowns in Sunday's 31-24 loss to the Lions. He added 12 rushing yards on two carries and threw a two-point conversion.
1373.long: The veteran QB was almost flawless as the Jets nearly pulled off the upset, with his only turnover being a fumble on his fifth sack of the day late in the fourth quarter, ending his final possession. Smith spread the ball around, completing passes to eight different targets and connecting with Garrett Wilson, Jeremy Ruckert and rookie first-round pick Kenyon Sadiq for his scores. Smith has been extremely efficient to begin the season, posting a 75.5 percent completion rate (77-for-102) with a 4:0 TD:INT and 7.7 YPA. He'll look to stay sharp in a Week 4 road trip to Chicago.

8146.short: Wilson caught 10 of 13 targets for 107 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 31-24 loss to Detroit.
8146.long: The star wideout -- who was evaluated for a head injury and cleared to return -- paced Jets pass catchers in all three receiving categories, and his 23-yard TD from Geno Smith in the fourth quarter tied the game at 24-24, only for the Lions to respond inside the final two minutes. It's Wilson's first 100-yard performance since Week 14 of the 2024 season, as injuries disrupted his 2025 campaign. Wilson also has found the end zone in back-to-back games, and he'll take a 21-243-2 line on 27 targets into a Week 4 road trip to Chicago.

11755.short: Stiggers (hand) returned to Sunday's game versus the Lions, Brian Costello of the New York Post reports.
11755.long: Stiggers exited the contest after suffering a hand injury early in the first quarter. However, it appears the injury wasn't anything serious, though his return mostly impacts the special-teams unit while adding depth to the secondary.

7678.short: Ossai (foot) is active for Sunday's game against the Lions.
7678.long: Ossai was trending in the right direction for Week 3 after logging a full practice Friday, and the veteran pass rusher has been given the green light to play Sunday after going through pregame warmups. It will be Ossai's 2026 regular-season debut, and he's expected to serve in a rotational role at defensive end behind starters Will McDonald and Kingsley Enagbare.

12925.short: The Jets signed Pritchett from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday, Zack Rosenblatt of The Athletic reports.
12925.long: The Jets signed Pritchett to the practice squad Sept. 2 after waiving the wide receiver on cutdown day. The second-year player out of South Alabama has yet to play in an NFL contest. If Adonai Mitchell (finger) cannot suit up for Sunday's game against the Lions, Pritchett is set to be the No. 4 option for the Jets in his debut.

3200.short: The Jets elevated Shepard from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday, Zack Rosenblatt of The Athletic reports.
3200.long: Shepard is set to suit up as the No. 6 wide receiver for the Jets in Sunday's game against the Lions. The new practice squad face was elevated for a scenario where Adonai Mitchell (finger) is unable to play in Sunday's contest. If Mitchell receives the green light, Shepard may spend his first elevation with the team inactive.

5119.short: The Jets elevated Sanders from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday, Zack Rosenblatt of The Athletic reports.
5119.long: Sanders will once again be the Jets' primary kicker for the third consecutive week and is set to suit up for Sunday's game against the Lions. The 30-year-old has now seen all three of his practice squad elevations expended, meaning he will need to be signed to the Jets' active roster to kick for the team in Week 4 against the Bears.

12539.short: Smith (knee) underwent surgery Wednesday to repair a torn ACL and will miss the rest of the season, Antwan V. Staley of the New York Daily News reports.
12539.long: Smith suffered a knee injury during the 20-17 overtime loss to Green Bay in Week 2. He will finish the 2026 campaign without a catch (one target), adding four carries for 13 yards. With Smith, Omar Cooper (ankle) and Tim Patrick (groin) out of the equation, Isaiah Williams could be in line for more opportunities behind Adonai Mitchell and Garrett Wilson. The Jets also signed Malik McClain off the practice squad Tuesday, which will help fill some of the void left by the injuries within the receiving corps.

3281.short: Onyemata (groin) underwent core-muscle surgery Wednesday, Antwan V. Staley of the New York Daily News reports.
3281.long: Onyemata was injured during the 20-17 overtime loss to Green Bay in Week 2. He was placed on the injured reserve list Tuesday, and while that means he will miss at least four games, he is anticipated to be out longer, though head coach Aaron Glenn expects him back before the end of the season. While Onyemata is out of commission, Darrell Jackson, Jowon Briggs, T'Vondre Sweat and Harrison Phillips will presumably see more snaps in each game moving ahead.

1052.short: Davis posted four tackles (three solo) during the Jets' 20-17 overtime loss to the Packers on Sunday.
1052.long: Davis was one of six Jets players to play all 59 defensive snaps during Sunday's OT loss. The veteran linebacker is up to 12 total tackles through two games and on pace to crack 100 tackles for a 10th straight year and the 13th time in his NFL career. He should stay busy Week 3 against the Lions on Sunday.

7841.short: Sherwood posted six tackles (three solo) and a pass defense during the Jets' 20-17 overtime loss to the Packers on Sunday.
7841.long: Sherwood was working through a minor knee issue during Week 2 prep, but he managed to play every single defensive snap during Sunday's OT loss and finished tied with Dane Belton for the most tackles on the Jets. Sherwood is up to 10 total tackles through two games, and he's currently behind pace to reach the 100-tackle mark for a third consecutive year. He'll have his hands full in the Jets' Week 3 road tilt against the Lions on Sunday.

6353.short: The Jets signed Reeder off the practice squad Tuesday.
6353.long: Reeder played 25 snaps on special teams as a standard elevation in Sunday's overtime loss to the Packers. He's now got a spot on the 53-man roster and will serve as a depth linebacker and special-teams piece for Gang Green.

11571.short: Davis didn't have any output in the box score during the Jets' overtime loss to the Packers on Sunday.
11571.long: Davis didn't see any playing time on offense for the second straight week, as Breece Hall and Braelon Allen once again handled the ground attack. While the 24-year-old did manage to record a tackle across his 22 special-teams snaps, he will likely continue to serve in a limited role unless Hall or Allen gets hurt.

6900.short: Greenard (pectoral) is listed as questionable ahead of Monday's game against the Bears.
6900.long: Greenard was a full participant in Saturday's practice, marking the first time the linebacker has achieved that level of participation since sustaining his pectoral injury. Despite practicing in full, Greenard remains questionable to suit up for Monday's contest as the team makes certain the 29-year-old is ready for the challenge.

5848.short: Brown (ankle) has been ruled out ahead of Monday's game against the Bears.
5848.long: Brown suffered an ankle injury during Week 3 prep and has been unable to practice since sustaining the injury. The wide receiver will officially not be suiting up for Monday's game, leaving Darius Cooper to be the No. 4 wide receiver behind DeVonta Smith, Dontayvion Wicks and Makai Lemon.

11577.short: Shipley (foot) was a limited participant in Saturday's practice but does not carry an injury designation into Monday's game against the Bears.
11577.long: Shipley ended the week with back-to-back limited practices while working through a foot injury, but he's been officially cleared to play for MNF. Saquon Barkley (shoulder) and Tank Bigsby (abdomen) have also been cleared to play, so Shipley will serve as the Eagles' third option out of the backfield.

9225.short: Bigsby (abdomen) does not carry an injury designation into Monday's game against the Bears.
9225.long: Bigsby was working through an abdominal injury throughout the week, but he faded an injury tag after logging a full practice Saturday. He worked in an elevated role on offense against the Titans in Week 2, but Bigsby will be the Eagles' RB2 for Monday after Saquon Barkley was able to overcome a shoulder stinger. Will Shipley (foot) will serve as the third option out of the backfield.

5022.short: Goedert (knee) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Bears.
5022.long: Goedert was unable to practice all week due to an MCL sprain that he sustained during the Eagles' Week 2 win over the Titans. Zach Ertz was signed to the Eagles' practice squad Tuesday, and he figures to be elevated to the active roster for Monday's game and provide depth at tight end behind Johnny Mundt and E.J. Jenkins. Goedert's next chance to play is Week 4 against the Rams on Sunday, Oct. 4, though he should be considered week-to-week.

7525.short: Smith (hamstring) is participating in Saturday's practice, Dave Zangaro of NBC Sports Philadelphia reports.
7525.long: Smith has been working through a hamstring injury, which prevented him from practicing Thursday before he returned for Friday's session in a limited capacity. His status for Monday night's game against the Bears will be more clear once the Eagles announce their injury designations following Saturday's practice. Smith is coming off a 10-117-1 receiving line (on 13 targets) against the Titans in Week 2, and if he were to be ruled out or limited against Chicago, then Dontayvion Wicks, Makai Lemon and Darius Cooper would all be in line for more targets from Jalen Hurts.

12604.short: Mukuba (knee) was a full participant in Friday's practice.
12604.long: Mukuba was a full participant in Friday's practice after being limited in Thursday's session. The safety appears to be over the knee injury that plagued him throughout Week 2. Mukuba will likely head into Monday night's game against the Bears healthy and without any injury designation.

10888.short: Carter (wrist) was a full participant in Friday's practice.
10888.long: Carter logged a limited practice session Thursday before upgrading to full participation Friday. The defensive tackle appears to be over the wrist injury that he played through in the Eagles' Week 2 win over the Titans. There is a strong chance Carter heads into Monday night's matchup with the Bears fully healthy and clear of any injury designation.

4866.short: Barkley (stinger) was a full practice participant Friday.
4866.long: Barkley's status for Week 3 was chief among the health concerns coming out of a Week 2 win at Tennessee in which he suffered a stinger and missed most of the first half. After kicking off this week with a limited practice Thursday, he handled every practice rep one day later, indicating he's good to go for Monday's contest in Chicago. Having said that, Barkley told Dave Zangaro of NBC Sports Philadelphia on Friday that he'll wear protective gear around his neck and shoulders this week and perhaps as long as symptoms of the stinger are impacting him.

13150.short: Cooper caught two of three targets for 26 yards and a touchdown in the Eagles' 24-20 win over the Titans on Sunday.
13150.long: With Dallas Goedert (knee) going down early in the game, Cooper played 31 offensive snaps as the No. 4 receiver after logging just eight in Week 1 against the Commanders. Cooper responded to the increased playing time by breaking free in the back of the end zone with nine seconds left in the fourth quarter to catch the game-winning three-yard touchdown from Jalen Hurts. Cooper doesn't carry much value in redraft fantasy leagues and would need an injury or two ahead of him at the position for that to change.

4314.short: Mundt caught two of three targets for eight yards in Sunday's 24-20 win against the Titans.
4314.long: Mundt started along with fellow tight end Dallas Goedert (knee), and he logged 49 of Philadelphia's 76 offensive snaps. The significant playing time was partly due to Goedert exiting in the first half after spraining his MCL. Goedert is now slated to miss multiple weeks due to the injury, but that won't necessarily mean that Mundt will be an attractive fantasy waiver-wire pickup. The Eagles signed veteran Zach Ertz to a contract Tuesday, and he'll likely slide in as the team's top tight end during Goedert's absence, though it's unclear how long Ertz will need to get up to speed.

6815.short: Baun recorded four total tackles (two solo) during Sunday's 24-20 win over Tennessee.
6815.long: Baun matched his season low in tackles from the 2025 campaign Sunday, but he was still on the field for all 53 of the team's defensive snaps in the contest. He has now compiled 16 total tackles (nine solo) and two passes defensed over two games this season. The linebacker will likely be more involved against the Bears on Monday Night Football in Week 3.

12566.short: Campbell recorded 10 total tackles (six solo) and a forced fumble during Sunday's 24-20 win over the Titans.
12566.long: Campbell was able to notch double-digit takedowns for the first time this season, and he stripped running back Tyjae Spears in the second quarter, but the ball went out of bounds before it could be recovered. The linebacker has now compiled 19 total tackles (11 solo), including 1.0 sacks, and a forced fumble over two games this year.

1339.short: Ertz signed with the Eagles' practice squad Tuesday, Chris McPherson of the team's official site reports.
1339.long: Adam Schefter of ESPN reported Monday that the 35-year-old Ertz would sign with the Eagles as a member of the practice squad, and that was confirmed a day later. Ertz, who won his lone Super Bowl ring and earned each of his three Pro Bowl nods as a member of the Eagles from 2013 through 2021, may need some time to get back up to full speed after tearing his ACL last December and then not participating in training camp with a team. Once he's fully ramped up, Ertz could settle in as the Eagles' top tight end with Dallas Goedert (knee) facing a multi-week absence and with Eli Stowers (quadriceps/hamstring) and Grant Calcaterra (back) already on injured reserve.

4195.short: Elliott converted his only field-goal attempt and made all three of his PATs in Sunday's 24-20 win over the Titans.
4195.long: Elliott made the most of his lone field-goal try of the day, making a 58-yarder in the third quarter. The kicker hasn't been leaned on often so far this year, but he has made both of his field-goal tries, and Sunday's 58-yard make is rather inspiring after Elliott combined to make five of 15 attempts from 50-plus yards over the last two seasons.

13294.short: Lemon caught his lone target for 14 yards while turning one carry into minus-5 yards during the Eagles' 24-20 win over the Titans on Sunday.
13294.long: Lemon recorded minus-5 receiving yards on three catches during his NFL debut against the Commanders in Week 1.
